title: Customers Who Never Made a Second Purchase
description: Find all customers who placed **exactly one order** and never returned. Return their customer_id and the date of their single order. These are the one-time buyers who churned immediately.
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS order_date FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: Customers 3, 5, 7, 8 each have exactly one order. Customers 1, 4, 6 have multiple orders and are excluded.

hints: GROUP BY customer_id and count their orders — the key is HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 to keep only those with a single order.
Since a one-time buyer has exactly one order, MIN(order_date) = that single date, giving you the purchase date cleanly.
explanation: Grouping by customer_id lets COUNT(*) tally orders per customer. HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 filters to one-time buyers. C1 has 2 orders, C4 has 3, C6 has 2 — all excluded. C3, C5, C7, C8 appear exactly once → 4 results. Since each has only one record, MIN(order_date) simply returns that date. This analysis is the first step in studying purchase retention rates.
